correctness.rationale: The event probability is exactly 6/[n(n-1)] per specified consecutive triple. Pairwise overlap event probabilities have three exact block-contraction cases and sum to O(n^-2), giving P(C_n>=1)=6/n+O(n^-2) and uniqueness under conditioning. Conditional on any one block, a uniform six-element-order mark is independent of the contracted uniform permutation. All mixed factorial moments of external oriented adjacency counts tend uniformly to one, hence two independent Poisson(1) limits; at most two boundary pair events disappear with probability O(1/n). Transferring from a marked to an existing block has relative O(1/n) bounded-test error. A standalone exhaustive exact verifier confirms all required finite identities through n=8 (46,230 permutations, 230 assertions); finite checks do not prove the limit.

originality.rationale: The new theorem gives the rare-event conditional joint law of increasing/decreasing common adjacency counts, including an independent Poisson background plus a correlated four-point mark. Fully inspected primary Section 2 in Corteel–Louchard–Pemantle gives separate marginal Poisson and three-block-frequency laws; Xu–Alain–Sankoff provides marginal adjacency laws. Neither inspected source derives the conditional marked law, and those marginal statements cannot imply it. Actual semantic literature-index queries found related but noncovering work; priority remains qualified rather than certified unique.
residual_risks: Older Kaplansky–Wolfowitz run-count work and historical genome-comparison literature might contain a differently named selected rare-run law not indexed by available searches.
The publisher HTML representation of Xu–Alain–Sankoff contains images instead of some formulas; no conclusion relies on a missing formula or an uninspected complete PDF.
Search of published research findings can miss synonymic prior results and does not by itself certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: Conditioning on a shared consecutive three-marker block is a natural genomic-selection event. It necessarily forces one or two common adjacencies, with a four-point sign-dependent mark and an independent Poisson background. The full limiting conditional joint null distribution materially changes significance calibration for selected genomes and is not just a textbook restatement of Poisson(2) marginals. The source paper motivates common intervals through gene-cluster detection and the second motivates probabilistic adjacency significance testing.
